subject: dhole
title: A 40-Pound Wild Dog Hunts Deer Ten Times Its Size by Whistling

scenes.text: In Asia's forests, hunters whistle to each other. They aren't human.
Dholes are wild dogs that weigh about 26 to 44 pounds, smaller than many pet dogs.
They live in packs, usually five to twelve, sometimes thirty or more.
In thick jungle where they can't see each other, they keep in touch with sharp whistles.
Working together, a pack can bring down a sambar deer about ten times the size of one dog.
Alone, it's a small dog. Whistling as a team, it's one of Asia's top hunters.

description:
Dholes, the 'whistling dogs' of Asia, weigh about 12 to 20 kg (26 to 44 lb) and hunt in packs, usually of 5 to 12 and sometimes 30 or more.
They keep in contact in dense forest with distinctive whistles, and a pack can take down sambar deer about ten times the size of one dhole.
Had you ever heard of the dhole?
first_comment: Dholes whistle to hunt as a team. Which pack hunter do you think is the deadliest?
